articles.author: Socialist Forum
articles.content_excerpt: American politics is at a crossroads. All that was once considered certain or possible is now in question. For the first time since the early 20th century, American Socialists are gaining considerable municipal and state level influence through successful and highly publicized electoral campaigns. After a largely successful midterm showing, the DSA established itself as a small but potent force in American politics. For the first time there is a comparatively large cohort of elected DSA members holding local, state, and federal office. Along with this heightened political influence comes greater political risk. articles.author: Oskar Brandt
articles.content_excerpt: After prices began rising and rising in the wake of COVID-19 and Russia’s invasion of Ukraine, some blamed welfare and public spending for the inflation. In the United States, changes to trade policy during Donald Trump’s first presidency added to uncertainty about the economic situation. articles.title: Anwar Shaikh Renewed Marx’s Economic Theory for Our Time
articles.author: Riccardo Bellofiore
articles.content_excerpt: Anwar Shaikh, who died on October 6, 2026, was one of the most original economists of the last half-century. Few did as much to rescue the Marxian critique of political economy from its theoretical difficulties and develop it into a rigorous, empirically grounded analysis of contemporary capitalism. Shaikh’s ambition was extraordinary. He reconstructed classical political economy as an alternative to the neoclassical mainstream, understanding capitalism not as a system tending toward harmonious equilibrium but as a turbulent social order whose normal functioning generates competition, conflict, structural change, and crisis. The affordability issues that drove the midterm elections weren’t mitigated by the mere fact of a blue wave. Democratic leaders in Congress and the individual states still face systemic problems, some of which can appear intractable. California’s poverty rate is among the highest in the nation, as it has been for nearly 15 years. articles.author: Detroit DSA
articles.content_excerpt: Our classrooms have been flooding multiple times a year. As demoralized as my co-workers were, this issue had the juice we needed to lead a workplace action — everyone cared enough to do something about it. Once boiling hot water sprayed out of the HVAC unit during class, nearly injuring a student. articles.title: Amazon Is Ratcheting Up Its Fight With NYC Delivery Drivers
articles.author: Alex N. Press
articles.content_excerpt: New Yorkers opening Amazon’s app on Thursday were greeted with a warning: “NYC Council could add up to $5 per order.” A link invited them to “act now to protect low prices,” directing customers to contact their city council members about legislation that would require Amazon to directly employ its delivery drivers. Amazon rolled out the warnings, which also appear on packages delivered in the New York area, as part of its campaign against New York City’s Delivery Protection Act (DPA), which an Amazon-funded coalition has already spent upward of $8 million opposing. Amazon is warning customers that the legislation would put small delivery companies out of business, eliminate jobs, and delay their packages. articles.title: The Jensen Huang Scandal: A Gift to China Hawks and AI Giants
articles.author: Branko Marcetic
articles.content_excerpt: Often, when people cheat on their spouses, they get kicked out of the house and strain their families. Not many can say they wiped out $1.8 trillion worth of share value and made the economy wobble. Yet this is exactly the case with ousted Nvidia chief executive officer Jensen Huang and the scandal surrounding his various infidelities, including to a woman who is allegedly a Chinese spy. (Or is she?) The uncertainty around that question is part of the general murkiness of this entire affair (no pun intended), one tied into a knot of three separate political threads: the economy’s outsize reliance on the artificial intelligence industry, ruthless corporate anti-competition, and the simmering new Cold War with China.
